description: This data set is a synthetic transmission grid test case for Ghana in West Africa, one of very few open grid models for the region. It was published on Zenodo in 2025 by Richard Asiamah for power system studies, algorithm benchmarking, regional research and teaching. Built from publicly available data and methods from earlier synthetic grid work, it aims to be realistic but not real. The first version represented each substation as a single bus to form the topological skeleton; the second version, from June 2025, adds multiple buses per substation joined by transformers between nominal voltage levels, which increases the numbers of buses and lines while leaving generation and demand profiles unchanged. Coverage is the national grid of Ghana. The file is a single MATPOWER case, downloadable from Zenodo under CC BY 4.0 at no cost. Caveats: the grid is synthetic, so it should not be used to describe actual Ghanaian assets, and bus and line counts are not given in the abstract. Simulation uses are power flow and optimal power flow studies for West African grid planning. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day.
